title: The Edge of Knowing
statement: Earthrise is the distant fact; the city and the witness are records. Plants and portraits become acts of inference when displaced, while the flowering bestiary marks what cannot be securely named. The gaps between these fragments are part of the evidence.
brief:
Create an original collage using only the provided source images. There is no target image. Respond to the condition through the composition itself. Give the finished work a title and a short artist statement.

Represent the boundary between what you know, what you infer, and what you cannot know.

actions.title: The Edge of Knowing
actions.statement: Earthrise is the distant fact; the city and the witness are records. Plants and portraits become acts of inference when displaced, while the flowering bestiary marks what cannot be securely named. The gaps between these fragments are part of the evidence.

notes.error: Use a boolean done and at most 12 actions; an empty batch is allowed only when done is true or reviewOnly is true.

notes.note: Build the collage in a clear hierarchy: Earthrise as the dark field of what can be observed, the city as recorded structure, botanical and portrait fragments as inference, and the hybrid bestiary as the unresolved zone between categories.

actions.title: The Edge of Knowing
actions.statement: Earthrise is the distant fact; the city and the witness are records. Plants and portraits become acts of inference when displaced, while the flowering bestiary marks what cannot be securely named. The gaps between these fragments are part of the evidence.

notes.note: The first arrangement establishes a strong vertical axis, but the rectangular source edges make the inferred and unknowable zones too literal. I will introduce irregular silhouettes and one additional red observational fragment so the boundary feels constructed rather than merely layered.

The canvas now reads as a staged epistemic field: the city is the documented anchor, the portraits and botanical form are conjectural witnesses, and the bestiary/flamingo occupy the uncertain upper space. I will add a narrow historical crowd fragment as a visual threshold between ground and sky, plus a small theatrical fragment to intensify the distinction between record and performance.

The visual hierarchy is working: Earthrise and the city establish fact, while the separated botanical, portrait, flamingo, and bestiary fragments inhabit progressively less certain space. I will add one small reflective artifact in the open upper field as a quiet marker of self-observation, then inspect the revised balance before finishing.

The final inspection shows a finished composition: the lunar ground and city establish observable fact, the portrait and botanical forms suggest interpretation, and the floating bestiary, flamingo, theatrical poster, and reflective artifact occupy the unknowable. The open black field and visible gaps make the boundary itself part of the work.
